text.p: These are leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zambia National Union of Teachers has blamed a spate of public service strikes on opposition parties. Union chief Mwembe Sichone said the United National Independence Party and Zambia Democratic Congress were encouraging workers to strike.
- Parliament on Wednesday rejected a government bill to shut down the cash-strapped Development Bank of Zambia and replace it with another bank within five years.
- Council workers in the mining town of Kitwe have refused to join in a strike started by their counterparts in the neighbouring town of Ndola.
- The Southern African National Institute for Economic Policy has said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has tailored Structural Adjustment programmes for the spread of AIDS in Southern Africa.
